profile_summary.name: Meera
profile_summary.bmi_note: Just over the 25.0 line. For a lifter this overstates fatness; judge progress by the waist tape, the 7-day scale average, and how the lifts hold — not the BMI number alone.
profile_summary.current_lifts_note: Starting loads below are set from what you already lift: goblet squat 20 kg x 10, DB bench 17.5 kg x 10, RDL 40 kg x 8. Each session lists the working weight to open with.
profile_summary.bmr_equation: Mifflin-St Jeor for a 32-year-old woman, 168 cm, 72 kg: 10x72 + 6.25x168 - 5x32 - 161 = 1470 kcal.
profile_summary.activity_factor_note: BMR x 1.4 for a desk job plus the step target lands maintenance near 2050 kcal.
profile_summary.calorie_adjustment_note: A 400 kcal deficit targets about 0.5 percent of bodyweight lost per week - fast enough to see, slow enough to keep strength and muscle.
assumptions: You can train three days a week with dumbbells, a barbell and a bench.
No injuries or dietary restrictions were reported, so nothing is excluded.

weekly_split.frequency_rationale: Three full-body days beat a bro-split on a deficit: every muscle is trained often enough to signal 'keep me' while total fatigue stays low, which is what protects muscle while you lose fat.

days.focus: Full body A - squat and press emphasis
Rest, plus a 25 minute walk and the daily step target
Full body B - hinge and pull emphasis
Rest, plus a 25 minute walk and the daily step target
Full body C - lunge and upper emphasis

weekly_split.scheduling_note: Keep a day between sessions so each one is fresh. If a day slips, train Mon-Thu-Sat instead - never two hard days back to back.

workout_days.day_label: Full body A - squat and press (Monday)
workout_days.warmup: 5 minutes easy cardio, then 2 light ramp sets of the goblet squat and the press.

exercises.name: Goblet squat
exercises.tempo_or_notes: Open at 20 kg. Add 2.5 kg once you hit 12 reps on every set with clean depth.
exercises.substitution: Leg press or dumbbell box squat

exercises.name: Dumbbell bench press
exercises.tempo_or_notes: Open at 17.5 kg per hand, 2 second lowering, no bounce.

exercises.name: Chest-supported row
exercises.tempo_or_notes: Open at 12.5 kg per hand. Squeeze the shoulder blades, no torso swing.

exercises.name: Seated dumbbell shoulder press
exercises.tempo_or_notes: Open at 10 kg per hand. Stop one rep short of a grinder.

exercises.name: Plank
exercises.tempo_or_notes: Ribs down, glutes tight. Add time before adding load.

workout_days.session_notes: This is the heaviest day - it comes first while you are fresh.

workout_days.day_label: Full body B - hinge and pull (Wednesday)
workout_days.warmup: 5 minutes easy cardio, then 2 light ramp sets of the RDL.

exercises.name: Romanian deadlift
exercises.tempo_or_notes: Open at 40 kg. Hips back, soft knees, feel the hamstrings - not the lower back.

exercises.name: Lat pulldown
exercises.tempo_or_notes: Open at a weight you control for 12. Lead with the elbows.

exercises.name: Walking lunge
exercises.tempo_or_notes: Bodyweight to start, then hold 5 kg per hand. Long stride, tall torso.

exercises.name: Dumbbell incline curl
exercises.tempo_or_notes: Open at 6 kg per hand. Slow lowering, no swing.

exercises.name: Hanging or lying leg raise
exercises.tempo_or_notes: Control the way down. Stop when the lower back wants to arch.

workout_days.session_notes: Posterior-chain focus balances the pressing from Monday.

workout_days.day_label: Full body C - lunge and upper (Friday)
workout_days.warmup: 5 minutes easy cardio, then 2 light ramp sets of the split squat.

exercises.name: Bulgarian split squat
exercises.tempo_or_notes: Bodyweight to start, then hold 7.5 kg per hand. Front foot flat, drive through the heel.

exercises.name: Incline dumbbell press
exercises.tempo_or_notes: Open at 12.5 kg per hand on a low incline.

exercises.name: Single-arm dumbbell row
exercises.tempo_or_notes: Open at 15 kg. Brace on the bench, pull to the hip.

exercises.name: Lateral raise
exercises.tempo_or_notes: Open at 5 kg per hand. Lead with the elbows, no shrug.

exercises.name: Triceps rope pushdown
exercises.tempo_or_notes: Open light, full lockout, slow return.

workout_days.session_notes: Lighter and quicker - the week ends on a pump, not a grind.

progressive_overload.method: Double progression inside a deficit: add reps first, load only when the top of the range is clean.
protocol: Hit the top of the rep range on every set of an exercise before adding weight.
When you do, add the smallest jump (2.5 kg lower body, 1-2.5 kg upper) and rebuild the reps.
On a cut, holding your loads week to week already counts as winning - you are keeping muscle while losing fat.
progressive_overload.load_increments: Lower body 2.5 kg, upper body 1 to 2.5 kg, isolation 1 kg or one more rep.
progressive_overload.deload: Every 6 weeks, or sooner if two lifts stall in the same week: halve the sets and take 15 to 20 percent off the loads for one week.
progressive_overload.tracking: Log the working weight and reps each session so the check-in can read the trend, not your memory.

quality_vs_quantity.stance: On a cut, less is more.
quality_vs_quantity.why: Recovery is lower when you eat less, so the goal is the least training that keeps muscle - not the most you can survive.
practical_rules: Leave 1 to 2 reps in reserve on the compounds; the deficit is the fat-loss driver, not gym punishment.
Protect sleep and protein first; they decide whether the scale drop is fat or muscle.
If a session feels awful, cut a set or two rather than skipping - showing up keeps the habit.

rationale.goal_fit: Three full-body days give high training frequency at low weekly fatigue, which is the muscle-sparing setup for a cut.
rationale.exercise_selection: Compounds first for the biggest muscle signal per minute, then a little targeted arm and shoulder work so the parts you see in the mirror hold up.
rationale.ordering: Heaviest day Monday while fresh; posterior chain Wednesday; a lighter, quicker session Friday.
rationale.volume_analysis: Weekly direct sets land near the lower-middle of the intermediate band - about 8 to 11 per muscle - which is the right dose to keep muscle on a deficit rather than chase growth you cannot fuel.

cardio_and_steps.step_rationale: Steps burn fat without eating into gym recovery the way hard cardio does. Nudging from 5000 to 8500 adds a meaningful daily deficit you barely feel.

cardio_sessions.placement: on rest days or after a session

cardio_and_steps.interference_note: Keep hard cardio minimal on a cut - walking and steps do the job without stealing recovery from the lifts.

diet_plan.macro_rationale: Protein is set high at about 1.9 g per kg to protect muscle in the deficit. Fat sits at a healthy floor for hormones; carbs take the rest and fuel the sessions.

meal_schedule.timing_note: protein plus vegetables to finish full

foods: 3 egg whites plus 1 whole egg scramble
a big mixed salad with 1 tsp olive oil

sample_day_totals.note: Hit protein and calories; swap foods you dislike for ones you enjoy with the same numbers.

diet_plan.pre_post_workout: No special timing needed - just make sure lunch or a protein snack lands within a few hours of training.
diet_plan.hydration: Aim for 2 to 2.5 litres of water a day; hunger is often thirst on a cut.
diet_plan.diet_preference_note: Vegetarian swaps: paneer, tofu, dal and Greek yogurt cover the protein targets easily.
diet_plan.allergy_note: No allergies were reported, so nothing is excluded. Adjust if that changes.

supplements.name: Creatine monohydrate
supplements.why: Helps hold strength and muscle in a deficit; timing does not matter.

supplements.name: Whey or a plant protein
supplements.why: A convenience tool, not magic - real food first.

supplements_excluded_note: Fat burners and detox teas are skipped - they do nothing a deficit and steps do not already do.

duration_and_paths.review_points: Run the check-in every 4 weeks. Expect about 0.5 percent of bodyweight lost per week averaged over the block.
duration_and_paths.path_if_ahead: Losing faster than 1 percent a week or strength dropping? Add 100 to 150 kcal back - that is too aggressive.
duration_and_paths.path_if_behind: Scale flat for two weeks with good adherence? Trim about 150 kcal or add 1000 steps.

safety_notes: This is general fitness guidance, not medical advice. Stop and see a professional if a movement causes sharp pain. Very low intake plus heavy training is not the goal here - the deficit is moderate on purpose.
